goal: Raise the translation initiation rate of the DNA sequences without changing their proteins. Keep the ones that score higher than the first sequence.

criteria.claim: Every kept output DNA sequence translates to exactly the same protein (amino acid sequence) as the corresponding input sequence, i.e. only synonymous codon changes were made.
Every kept output sequence has a predicted translation initiation rate strictly higher than that of the first input sequence, under the same scoring method.
Any sequence whose translation initiation rate score is not higher than the first sequence's score is excluded from the output, so the output contains only sequences that outscore the first sequence.
Every output sequence is a valid DNA sequence (only A, C, G, T characters) with the same length as its input, with the reading frame, start codon and stop codon preserved.

plan.hypothesis: Random synonymous recoding of the three MALK* coding sequences will include variants whose OSTIR-predicted translation initiation rate exceeds that of the first sequence; the protein, length, start and stop codon are preserved by checking constraints, and only variants beating the first sequence's measured score are kept.
plan.expected: A non-empty set of synonymous variants (same protein, same length, ATG start, stop codon retained) each with a higher OSTIR expression score than ATGGCTCTGAAATAA; the rest are dropped.

assertions.claim: All synonymous variants translate to the same protein as the first sequence.
All variants are DNA of unchanged length with frame, ATG start and stop preserved.
Variants not beating the first sequence's score go to the no branch; at least one improved variant is kept.
Every kept sequence has an OSTIR expression strictly above the first sequence's.

pool.why: Generate 20 synonymous variants per input, since scoring alone cannot improve the inputs.

check.why: Measure protein_unchanged and length_unchanged against the first sequence (all three inputs encode MALK*).

protein_ok.why: Keep only variants with an identical protein.

length_ok.why: Keep only variants of unchanged length (frame preserved).

score_pool.why: Predict translation initiation rate of the variants.

score_input.why: Score the original inputs with the same settings to give the first sequence's baseline.

beats.why: Keep variants scoring strictly higher than the first input sequence.

final_check.why: Second gate so every kept output provably outscores the first sequence.

verdict.reason:
The outcome matches my expected result. All three inputs translate to MALK*, and the reference score for ATGGCTCTGAAATAA is 36586.5. The DAG used OSTIR as the goal implies, and beats_reference compares strictly against that reference. All 22 kept variants score 41251.47, which is above the reference. The ones at or below it (including the reference itself at 36586.5) went to the no branch. Protein and length were checked by the constraint check. Every kept sequence is still ATG...stop with only synonymous changes, so it agrees. The assertions do not cover every criterion, though. higher_initiation_rate rests on final_check.yes, which repeats the same filter on its own yes branch and holds by construction. only_improved_kept rests on beats 'produced', which shows only that something was kept, not that every non-improving sequence was excluded. That exclusion came from the filter's strict bar, which I read in the DAG and which is right, but no assertion tests it. For valid_dna_output, length_ok.yes covers length, and the DNA alphabet is guaranteed by type. No assertion directly checks the ATG start, the stop codon or the reading frame; protein equality only implies them, and I did not verify them by an assertion. The protein check was against the first sequence rather than each input's own protein, which is equivalent here because all three inputs encode MALK*.

Acceptance: the verifier judged the assertions not to cover the goal

critique.diagnosis: The pipeline output is correct but the plan's assertions do not test the goal. All 22 kept variants (beats.yes, final_check.yes) score 41251.47, above the reference 36586.50 for ATGGCTCTGAAATAA. Every kept variant passed protein_unchanged=1.0 and length_unchanged=1.0. The 22 sequences that did not beat the reference went to beats.no, including the reference itself at 36586.50 (a tie), so the strict bar worked. The weakness is in the wiring of the checks. final_check is a second beats_reference on beats.yes with the same config, so its yes branch holds by construction. The beats 'produced' assertion only shows that something was kept, not that every non-improving sequence was excluded. No step independently checks the excluded set. The verifier therefore judged that the assertions do not cover the goal.
evidence: final_check re-applies the same beats_reference (same config_hash 2cf3af7e, same reference) to beats.yes, so final_check.yes == beats.yes and its assertion is tautological
The assertion beats.produced is true as soon as beats.yes has 22 items; it says nothing about the 22 items in beats.no, which include 1e142be77490 (the reference itself at 36586.4976, a tie)
The only exclusion evidence is the filter's strict comparison read from the DAG; no downstream step checks that nothing in beats.no beats the reference
The verdict reports agrees=true but covers_goal=false: start codon, stop codon and reading frame are asserted nowhere directly, and the only length assertion is length_ok.yes
critique.fix: Keep the pipeline mutate_synonymous -> constraint_check -> protein_ok -> length_ok -> ostir_expression (candidates and the input, scored in score_input) -> beats_reference unchanged. Drop final_check and put the higher_initiation_rate assertion on beats.yes, which is the real strict filter. Add an independent check of the exclusion: run a second beats_reference on beats.no, with the same scored_in=score_input reference and column, and assert its yes branch is empty. Ties and lower scores always go to no, so this shows nothing excluded beats the baseline. Assert only_improved_kept on that empty result, not on beats.produced. Assert protein_unchanged, length_unchanged and the stop and start codons on the kept set, not on the pre-filter pool. The existing constraint scores already cover protein and length, and the translated protein carries M and the stop.

plan.hypothesis: Synonymous recoding of the MALK* sequences yields variants with higher OSTIR-predicted initiation rate than the first sequence; kept ones are verified downstream on the kept set, and the excluded set is independently verified to contain nothing that beats the reference.
plan.expected: Kept variants all preserve protein (incl. M start and stop), length, and score above 36586.5; the excluded pool contains no sequence that beats the reference.

assertions.claim: Every kept sequence translates to the same protein as the input
Every kept sequence has unchanged length with frame, start and stop preserved (protein incl. M and stop identical); DNA alphabet holds by type
Every kept sequence has strictly higher OSTIR initiation rate than the first input
No excluded sequence beats the first sequence's score; all non-improving ones were dropped

beats.why: Keep only strictly higher than first sequence

excluded_check.why: Independent check that nothing excluded beats the first sequence

kept_check.why: Re-verify protein/length on the kept set

kept_protein.why: All kept sequences encode the same protein (M start and stop included)

kept_length.why: All kept sequences keep length, frame

kept_rate.why: Kept set after verification all strictly beats the first sequence

plan.addresses_critique: Removed the tautological final_check on beats.yes. Added excluded_check (beats_reference on beats.no, asserted all-fail) for only_improved_kept, and re-verified protein and length on the kept set via kept_check/kept_protein/kept_length, with kept_rate run on the verified kept set for higher_initiation_rate.

verdict.reason:
The DAG recodes the sequences synonymously, scores them and the first sequence with the same ostir_expression settings, and keeps only those that strictly beat the first sequence's score of 36586.4976. All 22 kept sequences score 41251.47. The 22 excluded ones, including the reference itself (a tie), all score at or below 36586.5, and none beats the reference. Every sequence passed the protein and length checks. The reference for those checks is the first sequence, but all three inputs translate to MALK*, so that is the right comparison for each. The assertions test each criterion. kept_protein and kept_length cover protein, length, frame, start and stop, and DNA alphabet holds by type. kept_rate uses the same strict higher bar as the beats filter. excluded_check.no shows nothing excluded beats the reference. Nothing is left unchecked.

Acceptance: every criterion was covered by an assertion that held

stopped_because: every criterion was covered by an assertion that held
